newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Looters target wealthy Kinshasa suburbs.
newsitem.headline: Looters target wealthy Kinshasa suburbs.

text.p: Looting broke out in wealthy districts of Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Saturday as most areas of the vast city fell under rebel control, witnesses said.
The Binza area, home to Zaire's business and political elite, was the main target because Laurent Kabila's rebels had not yet reached it, they said.

State radio, captured by the rebels at 1.10 PM (1210 GMT), issued a warning about looting. "The areas of Telecom, Binza Pigeon and Binza IPN are victims of looting," an announcer said, breaking in to a programme of non-stop music.
Veteran politician Christophe Gbenye, who lives in Binza, told Reuters by telephone that mobs from neighbouring shanty towns began looting the houses of wealthy people in the morning.
"The looting is still going on. It's mainly young people who are looting big men's houses," he said. "The rebels have not arrived yet but when they do the looting will stop."
Other witnesses said hardline loyalists of ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko toured Binza with a double mission to loot and to eliminate certain members of the defeated regime.
The armed loyalists, mainly members Mobutu's presidential guard from his Ngbandi tribe, appeared to target personalities accused of appeasing Kabila or abandoning the fight.
Diplomats said defence minister General Mahele Lieko Bokungo, the army chief of staff killed overnight, was among the most prominent victims.
They also said they feared foreign minister Kamanda wa Kamanda was shot dead on Saturday by one of his bodyguards.
Central areas of Kinshasa were under full rebel control. They were reported calm and free of looting after tension earlier in the day as Mobutu's defeated troops retreated through the streets.
